analysis.title: Political interference at every corner
key_insights: EZ headline HICP is tracked at 3.7% YoY in November, down from 4.0% in October, after Brent fell EUR25/bl and TTF gas fell EUR12/MWh in a week on geopolitical de-escalation in Iran.

EZ core HICP was 2.54% YoY in October (2.50% in September). The rise came mainly from tourism-related services, which could partly reverse. Core goods rose only 2bp, so there is no spillover from energy so far.
The EZ core forecast for the 2027 average was cut by about 10bp to 2.9% YoY, and the 2028 average by 3-4bp to 2.3%, on lower gas prices easing production costs.

A granular PPI analysis shows little evidence of energy-crisis spillover to consumer prices. Manufacturing PPI rose from 0.3% YoY in February 2026 to 7.0% in September, while consumer goods PPI was 0.4% YoY. Food PPI was -1.9% YoY. Durable goods PPI rose 3.4% YoY, and furnishings PPI already shows in some countries' HICP.

Market expectations converged to the bank's forecast through end-2027 as energy fell. The bank has HICPx slightly below fixings from Q128 because it relies fully on strongly backwardated energy futures.

An LFI amendment to the 2027 French budget to end OATei/OATi issuance was adopted on 4 November, but the whole revenue section was then rejected unanimously. The 2027 budget will very likely pass via Article 49.3 or 47, so the usual linker issuance will almost certainly repeat in 2027. The bank expects more political interference on inflation in future.

Linker issuance could end in France only if an RN or LFI president is elected, the National Assembly backs the policy, the government sticks to it, and the fiscal situation allows it. The bank sees this as unlikely. A halt would force roughly EUR30bn more nominal OAT issuance, and French banks need OATi to hedge the Livret A (EUR600bn).

French PM Lecornu announced a 10-30% rise in the Livret A ceiling, from EUR22,950 to EUR25,000-30,000. The Livret A rate may rise to about 2.6% in February and about 2.8% in August. This should bring inflows and more need for French inflation hedging, so the bank closed its sell 3YF2Y FRCPIx vs HICPx trade, losing 3bp.

Eurozone inflation forwards (2YF2Y 1.99%, 5YFY 2.07%, 3YF2Y HICPx around 1.96%) are pricing zero inflation premium against core of about 2.9% in 2027 and 2.3-2.4% in 2028. The bank sees breakevens as increasingly attractive, helped by the end-November index extension and the usual linker supply slowdown after 20 November. Energy remains the first driver and market sentiment the second.

Jean-Luc Mélenchon's 2027 programme (about 15% minimum wage rise, wage indexation, price freezes on essentials) could add about 125bp to headline inflation over three years on the bank's estimate. His polling win probability is very low.

US October CPI (released the day of the report): the bank expects headline +0.29% MoM SA and core +0.26% MoM SA. That compares with 0.24% Bloomberg consensus and 0.33% in September. The 3mma annualised core would be 3.53%, the highest since January 2025. No YoY figure exists because the October 2025 index was never published, and fixings mark 3.54% YoY.

US midterm results are not a U-turn for US inflation. Crude is down from about USD110/bl to USD90/bl in two weeks on hopes of an Iran ceasefire, and this is already in the energy CPI path. The US chief economist sees policy gridlock persisting and no major fiscal package.

The US CPI path was cut and now sits in line with fixings for the rest of 2026 and 2027, slightly below market at Q328. Before, in September and October, it was 20-30bp below market for H227 and 2028. Core YoY will look stronger from November to February due to OER and rent base effects, then 2.5-2.7% for the rest of 2027.
The sell OATei Jul-47 breakeven vs BTPei Feb-46 trade stays open with P&L of about 5bp. 2026 trade ideas total 75bp P&L, down 4bp on the week, across 16 trades with a 63% hit ratio.

Germany stopped linker issuance after the 2022 inflation spike. Its programme was much smaller (EUR6-10bn a year) than France's (about EUR25bn a year). The 2027 Eurozone linker supply estimate is EUR51.2bn for ei and EUR67.2bn all-in.

risk_factors: Energy prices can surge again until the Strait of Hormuz situation is settled.
Re-escalation with Iran remains possible if Trump responds to the midterm defeat with greater assertiveness.
Tourism-related services strength in October core HICP could reverse or persist, and airfares may stay high as airline jet fuel hedges expire.
Political interference on inflation-linked issuance in France (LFI and RN opposition) and the 2027 presidential election risk.
The bank's HICPx sits below fixings from Q128 because it fully relies on backwardated energy futures.
The PPI pass-through to HICP is uncertain, and food and core goods inflation could be stronger than PPIs suggest because of input prices.
vol_and_positioning: Eurozone inflation forwards tightened, with 2YF2Y down 7bp to 1.99% and 5YFY down 3.5bp to 2.07% on the week, and the front end of the HICPx curve led the fall.

Inflation swaps and breakevens are seen as attractive from a contrarian view. Forwards near 2.0% imply zero inflation premium against the bank's core forecasts. Supportive technicals: end-November Bonosei-27 index extension and slower linker supply after 20 November.
geopolitical: Geopolitical de-escalation in Iran after the Democrats' midterm victory and talks with Qatar pushed Brent down EUR25/bl and TTF down EUR12/MWh in a week. A new energy surge remains possible until the Strait of Hormuz situation is settled.
US chief economist: Democrats will attempt to end the Iran conflict, but the President has greater ability to conduct foreign policy, and re-escalation remains possible.
French politics: LFI and RN oppose inflation-linked bonds, and Mélenchon's 2027 presidential programme includes minimum wage rises, wage indexation and price freezes.
US midterm blue wave: new Democratic governors in states like Texas and Ohio may slow data centre buildout, and gridlock limits fiscal packages.

tension_points.bull_case: Inflation forwards near 2.0% price zero inflation premium against core of about 2.9% in 2027 and 2.3-2.4% in 2028. Technicals are favourable: the strong end-November index extension and the usual linker supply slowdown after 20 November.
tension_points.bear_case: Energy remains the number one driver and market sentiment the number two. A fall in oil and gas continues to weigh on the HICPx curve, and the bank's own HICPx sits slightly below fixings from Q128.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A resolution of the Strait of Hormuz situation that keeps energy prices falling would keep pressure on breakevens. A renewed energy surge would support them.

tension_points.bull_case: The 2027 budget will very likely pass via Article 49.3 or 47, so OATei and OATi issuance will almost certainly repeat in 2027. Ending a EUR25bn programme would force about EUR30bn more nominal supply and create risks for French banks hedging the Livret A.
tension_points.bear_case: LFI and RN oppose linkers, and rising inflation makes their cost for public finances politically costly.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An RN or LFI president elected, with National Assembly support, a government sticking to its promise, and a fiscal situation allowing it.
